claims.source_claim: PBWM is source-inherited selective dopamine/BG-enabled gate over PFC stripes; model schematic not source new recorded BG dynamics
Input gating determines whether and which observed sensory category is written/updated into a working-memory stripe
Output gating prioritizes one stored WM representation to inform downstream action without writing the incoming input
Motor/response gating selects prepared response or maps selected maintained representation into an overt same/different response
Task experimenter independently manipulates update vs maintenance and switch vs repeat at three gating levels within reference-back-2; these are imposed cues not direct observed gate openings
Per-trial measured reaction times contrast gate switching and WM policy in N30 retained subjects, with N32 recruited/2 exclusions; regression/ANOVA inference differs from trial data

claims.locator: original complete S1 Text 5-factor full ANOVA
claims.source_claim: WM policy (update slower), input and output switch RT effects significant, response RT only marginal overall, under-additive pairwise and selected higher-order interactions
No overall error-rate main effects across all gating levels in full model; only specific WM×response, input×response and fourway error interactions significant
During updating only output switch has RT main effect, input/response do not; all pairwise under-additive but three-gate interaction not significant p=.21
During maintenance input/output/response all switch RT main effects and three pairwise plus three-way under-additive effects significant
Updating errors have input×response and three-way only, maintenance errors each main effects with input×response sole significant interaction; do not pool as universal effects

Observed EEG gate-switch-related scalp GLM activation temporal patterns partially overlap; posterior input-related P3b, frontal output-related N2, later response-related posterior slow wave are recorded electrode phenomena
The GLM traces, time-window correction/masks and independent electrode-decoder analyses are measurements bounded by sampled electrode potentials and task alignment; not causal BG observations

EEG multivariate evidence for task-category output reprioritization and motor-response priority relates predicted representation selection to measured task-dependent decoding; significance conditional on original mask and trial stratification
Fit hierarchical DDM separately condition-dependent boundary a, evidence drift v, nondecision t by Bayesian posterior and DIC comparisons among original nested candidate models
Posterior predictive RT density and QQ compare fitted hierarchical DDM to actual measured behavior; fit approximates empirical distribution with non-identical tails

The preferred original fitted model associates gate switching at each level with larger inferred boundary/decision threshold a; across co-occurring gate switches under-additive threshold combinations rather than strict sums
Estimated threshold highest-response-conflict prioritization depends on updating/maintenance and competition; an inferred control strategy is not directly a physiological striatal observation
Hierarchical DDM also estimates condition-related drift rate v differences; harder cognitive processing can lower v, competing a-only inference
Model fit not exact especially upper reaction-time tails, distributions and QQ plots are explicit source-native adverse quality limits
Parallel or under-additive hierarchy of gate activation and common cortico-striatal ancestral explanation remain explanatory hypotheses; time-varying drift/threshold competing variants not fitted
Current experimental gate/EEG/HDDM extension depends on Frank/O'Reilly/Badre prior PBWM and adapted cited older network figure; inherited mechanism cannot be claimed original independent invention
